name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the 7-day decay metric for top 20% prompts by usage. This keeps the system responsive by pruning stale high-usage prompts faster than a 30-day window, cutting wasted compute. The trade-off is losing some long-tail relevance for those prompts, but the gain in freshness outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: The 7-day decay metric risks overcorrecting—fresh regressions aren’t the only waste; silent failures in prompts still slip through. A rolling 30-day window with a *usage-weighted* decay (older prompts decay faster if underused) balances freshness and stability better. Settle it by measuring silent failure rates before and after both windows.
